newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares pierce 17,000, seen rising again.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares pierce 17,000, seen rising again.

text.p: Polish shares pierced the 17,000 barrier and set a second consecutive high in higher turnover on Friday, and analysts saw them setting a new record on Monday, but were not sure about the market's subsequent direction.

The main market's WIG index rose 543.7 points, or 3.2 percent, to 17,457.9, and turnover rose 24 percent to 256.3 million zlotys ($85.4 million) on both markets as 76 issues rose, five fell and seven were flat.

Analysts said the strong post-fixing buying during Friday's order balancing session signalled a rise of the WIG index on Monday, but said the gains could be limited as several stocks fell or stabilised during Friday's continuous trade.
"It's difficult to say what might happen next week, but Monday's session is likely to bring some growth," said Wojciech Kossuth, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.

Some analysts said that if the bourse continued to grow in jumps it could soon end up with violent falls of stocks which rose significantly during the last two months, which would pull the WIG index sharply down.
The bourse rose 8.4 percent this week.

Analysts said computer maker Optimus jumped 9.8 percent after it said it would convert 159 of its convertible bonds into shares, which would boost its January net profit by 1.3 million zlotys ($0.4 million).

Traders said mass privatisation NFI units soared 9.7 percent in a 46.9-million-zloty ($15.6 million) turnover in regular trade and rose 0.3 percent in 77.6-million-zloty ($25.9 million) continuous trade because of a buy recommendation from SBC Warburg in London.
Stock continuous trade amounted to 22.4 million zlotys ($7.5 million) with 11 stocks down, four up and six flat.
